hospitals.description: Morgan Stanley Children's Hospital is the Columbia side of NewYork-Presbyterian's children's program, sitting at Broadway and 165th Street in Washington Heights at the top of Manhattan. Its roots go back to Babies Hospital, founded in 1887, and the current building opened in 2003. It is a full quaternary referral center with a large PICU that includes a dedicated cardiac ICU, a level IV NICU, and one of the busiest pediatric ECMO programs in the world. The hospital is the only Level I pediatric trauma center in Manhattan and draws complex cardiac, transplant and neonatal patients from across the region and abroad. The surrounding neighborhood is dense and residential, with the George Washington Bridge and Fort Tryon Park close by.

hospitals.description: The Children's Hospital at Montefiore, known as CHAM, is a ten-story children's hospital attached to Montefiore's Moses campus in the Norwood section of the Bronx. Inside are a 26-bed PICU, a 35-bed AAP level III NICU, a 36-bed pediatric cardiology unit, a 28-bed adolescent unit and a 17-bed pediatric emergency department. The building is known for its space-themed design with NASA artifacts throughout. The neighborhood is residential and close to Mosholu Parkway and the Bronx River.

hospitals.description: Long Island Jewish Medical Center is Northwell Health's academic medical center on the Queens and Nassau line in New Hyde Park, and the campus that houses Cohen Children's Medical Center. It holds a NYS Regional Perinatal Center designation, with the Katz Women's Hospital and a high-level NICU run with Cohen's neonatology service. NYS DOH lists the pediatric and pediatric ICU beds under the LIJ license; those are described in the Cohen Children's record. This record is for adult, women's and newborn roles that post under LIJ rather than Cohen. The campus is suburban, off the Grand Central Parkway and Long Island Expressway.
